In the context of artificial intelligence, particularly in the field of natural language processing (NLP), "transformers" refer to a specific type of deep learning model architecture. This architecture was introduced in a groundbreaking paper titled "Attention is All You Need" in 2017. Transformers are designed to handle sequential data, such as text, and they have revolutionized the field of NLP by achieving state-of-the-art results on a wide range of tasks.

The key innovation of transformers is the use of self-attention mechanisms, which allow the model to weigh the importance of different words in a sentence when processing each word. This is a significant improvement over previous models that used recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, as transformers can process the input data in parallel, making them much faster to train.

Transformers have been used to develop a variety of models, including BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer), and T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer), among others. These models are pre-trained on large text corpora and can then be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as text classification, question answering, and language translation.

In summary, transformers are a powerful and flexible architecture in AI that has significantly advanced the capabilities of machines in understanding and generating human language.
